A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRR research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably across appendix moves and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PTQ and QPEFT experiments, including perplexity, downstream accuracy, training curves, ablations and rank-selection analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds effective-rank measurements, an ODLRI comparison and empirical assumption checks.

M1.justification: The preserve-quantize-reconstruct procedure, rank-selection criterion, optional rank-r reconstruction and QPEFT gradient scaling are unchanged. The new appendices evaluate and explain the existing method.

E1.justification: The training, calibration and evaluation datasets and tasks are retained, including WikiText2, the five PTQ downstream benchmarks, GLUE, SlimPajama and GSM8K. Added analyses reuse models and quantizers already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds ODLRI as an evaluated comparator in Appendix C.4/Table 16 on LLaMA-2 7B and LLaMA-3.1 8B. v1 cites the corresponding Cho et al. work but reports no ODLRI comparison. Existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New analyses measure dimension-normalized effective rank and evaluate assumptions using cross-layer CV and spectral-proxy MRE. Appendix E specifies LLaMA-2 7B with 3/4-bit MXINT, group size 32, and a GPTQ check. The ODLRI comparison uses QERA-exact, 3-bit MXINT and r=32; existing benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a targeted analysis of spectral structure across model scales, while Appendix E quantitatively checks the two assumptions underlying rank selection across bitwidths and quantizers. Existing rank-stability, reconstruction-alignment and gradient-scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing three-run mean/std reporting and the two-seed rank-stability analysis are unchanged. The new CV measures heterogeneity across layers as an evaluation diagnostic; no new repeated-run, confidence-interval, significance-testing or sampling-uncertainty procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. Table 16 adds ODLRI perplexities of 10.86 and 11.72 against SRR's 10.76 and 11.24, which already appear in Table 1. Table 15 adds effective-rank measurements; Tables 20–21 add CV/MRE results, including proxy MREs of 4.46% and 2.31% for 3/4-bit MXINT and 10.53% for GPTQ.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces the mathematical definition of the newly used entropy-based effective rank and its dimension normalization; Appendix E defines the new CV/MRE diagnostics. The original formal assumptions, error factorization and rank-selection derivation remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: allocating rank between preservation and reconstruction, theory-guided rank selection and stabilized QPEFT. The claimed 5.9-point average GLUE gain under 2-bit QPEFT is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains that fixed rank provides decreasing relative correction capacity as model width grows, interprets the ODLRI comparison as support for rank allocation beyond extraction, and suggests that channel-wise error accumulation explains GPTQ's larger spectral-proxy mismatch. These interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project-page address, providing access information absent from v1. Appendix A's implementation, calibration, hardware, computational-cost and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish what the linked page contains.

R1.justification: Appendix C.4 expands positioning against the already cited ODLRI work, distinguishing Hessian-informed extraction from rank-budget allocation. Appendix E adds the RPTQ citation, Yuan et al. (2023a), to support its GPTQ explanation. Other reference edits mainly concern formatting.

P1.justification: v2 lightly rewrites the introduction, adds acknowledgements and appendix subsections, and changes the publication footer. The former training-loss Appendix E becomes Appendix F. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact tables: 15, 16, 20 and 21. Former Tables 15–17 become Tables 17–19, while all nine figures retain their content. Appendix spacing, page placement and citation-link coloring also change.

improvement.justification: The ODLRI comparison, scale analysis and numerical assumption checks strengthen support and interpretation beyond v1's existing analyses. The gain is limited: Appendix E's cross-layer CV does not directly test Assumption 4.1's constancy across candidate residual matrices within a layer. Overall, v2 fills useful supporting-evidence gaps without substantially changing the established method or findings.
